subject.title: fix(mcp): honor `disabled` flag to prevent spawning disabled servers

question: Should MCP configuration continue to require canonical `enabled`, with legacy `disabled` handled only by Doctor migration, or should `disabled` become a supported public alias?
rationale: The current main schema and repository policy favor canonical runtime config plus Doctor-owned migration, while this PR intentionally expands the public configuration contract; that compatibility direction needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep canonical `enabled` only
options.body: Restore validation rejection for `disabled` and add or retain a narrow `openclaw doctor --fix` migration for any shipped legacy data.

options.title: Adopt a permanent alias
options.body: Define `enabled`/`disabled` precedence, strip or reject ambiguous pairs, canonicalize both boolean values on write, document the alias, and add fresh-install and upgrade coverage.

options.title: Pause the alias change
options.body: Keep the original report closed until concrete legacy input provenance demonstrates that a Doctor migration cannot cover the affected users.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical `enabled` only
recommendation.body: Restore validation rejection for `disabled` and add or retain a narrow `openclaw doctor --fix` migration for any shipped legacy data.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged MCP work provides the closest available history signal, although direct ownership of this configuration contract is not established.
